name: DNP cycle

card.summary: A DNP cycle is a short course of 2,4-dinitrophenol, an industrial chemical that raises body heat output, used by some to lose body fat quickly before a physique goal.
card.note: DNP has no antidote; overdose causes dangerous overheating and deaths have been reported.

quick.overview:
DNP (2,4-dinitrophenol) is an industrial chemical that was briefly sold as a weight-loss drug in the 1930s. Bodybuilders and people seeking rapid fat loss have used courses of it in recent decades, bought online, with the appearance goal of a lean physique in a few weeks.

It works as a mitochondrial uncoupler: energy that would be stored as ATP is released as heat, raising metabolic rate. Regulators and clinicians document serious harms, and forum users report weight changes alongside fever and heat symptoms.
quick.how: On looksmax.org, users post logs describing multi-week courses, often combined with calorie restriction, training and other fat-loss drugs, and report heat, sweating and fever. This article does not give doses or schedules.
quick.risks: DNP has a narrow therapeutic index; overdose can cause hyperthermia up to 44 C, tachycardia and death, and cataracts, vision loss and skin reactions have been reported. There is no antidote, and in 2023 the UK reclassified it as a regulated poison.

lead: A DNP cycle is the practice of taking 2,4-dinitrophenol, an industrial chemical, for a limited period to drive rapid fat loss, usually in bodybuilding and aesthetics circles aiming for a leaner look.[1]

DNP was used as a weight-loss drug in the 1930s, when Maurice Tainter of Stanford reported average losses of about 9.1 kg in 1933 and estimated that at least 100,000 Americans had been treated in the first year.[1] It acts as a protonophore, collapsing the mitochondrial proton gradient so that energy is lost as heat and metabolic rate rises.[1]

The 1938 Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act expanded FDA drug regulation and DNP was deemed too toxic for human consumption.[1] It is now sold online as a product, not an approved medicine, and forum users on looksmax.org post cycle logs and discuss combining it with other fat-loss compounds.[2][3]

chain: DNP uncouples mitochondria so energy leaves as heat
Faster body-fat reduction and a leaner look
angle.text: Users take DNP to burn more calories and lose body fat quickly. Forum logs report large weight drops over a few weeks, alongside heat and fever symptoms.

paras: During World War I, munitions workers in France fell ill, and some died, from DNP exposure.[1] Tainter published weight-loss results in 1933, and the AMA declined to list DNP in New and Nonofficial Remedies in 1935.[1] In 1936 a San Francisco ophthalmologist estimated 2,500 American women had gone blind from DNP use.[1] Loomis and Lipmann described its mechanism in 1948, and it was withdrawn from agricultural use in the US and Europe in 1998.[1]

Posts on looksmax.org include a 15-day experience thread in which the author reports losing about 19.6 pounds without exercise, with fever and intense heat in the first week,[2] and threads where users plan multi-week cycles alongside tirzepatide or testosterone.[3][4] One reply to the first thread says it is not that bad if hydrated, while another poster says he had heard it kills people.[2] A 2023 study cited by Wikipedia found commonly reported doses of 150 to 300 mg per day.[1]

The therapeutic index is narrow. Overdose can cause hyperthermia up to 44 C, tachycardia and death; cataracts, permanent vision loss, deafness, skin reactions and bone marrow effects have been reported.[1] Poison control cases between 2010 and 2020 had an 11.9% fatality rate, with at least 50 overdose deaths worldwide, and there is no antidote, only supportive care centred on aggressive cooling.[1]

WADA banned DNP in 2015, and Interpol and WADA issued an orange notice warning of its dangers.[1] A UK seller was convicted of manslaughter in 2018 and, after a retrial, of gross negligence manslaughter in 2020, and in October 2023 the UK reclassified DNP as a regulated poison.[1]
No studies found of modern DNP cycles for fat loss. Historical 1930s clinical use is described above.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, DNP cycles are posted as logs and planning threads, often with other fat-loss drugs.[2][3]

claims.claim: DNP gives very fast fat loss, nearly 20 lb in 15 days
claims.believers: One poster reports dropping from 192.4 to 172.8 pounds in 15 days with minimal exercise and one meal a day, and plans to continue.[2]
claims.experts: Historical studies reported average losses of about 9.1 kg in the 1930s, and regulators document fatal overheating and permanent injuries.[1]

claims.claim: Staying hydrated and avoiding summer makes it fine
claims.believers: A reply says it is not that bad if you avoid summer and stay hydrated.[2]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports no antidote, a narrow therapeutic index and deaths worldwide.[1]
